issues.title: Position-mode storage of a GTID source cannot serve a GTID replica
issues.summary: When the storage is in position mode but the source has gtid_mode=ON, the listener reports GTID_MODE=OFF (from the storage mode), so a MySQL replica with gtid_mode=ON refuses to start, although the stored binlogs carry the source's GTID events. MySQL 9.7 defaults to gtid_mode=ON.
issues.description: D35, `ReplicaOfPositionStorageOfGtidSourceMySQL`: the replica-of-listener property D7 with a position-mode storage of the gtid_mode=ON source; the replica (gtid_mode=ON, SOURCE_LOG_FILE / SOURCE_LOG_POS) stops at once with "The replication receiver thread cannot start because the source has GTID_MODE = OFF and this server has GTID_MODE = ON" (MY-013117). Sandbox and Jenkins #29.
issues.root_cause: Hrvoje's analysis (ticket 30, PBS-102): since PBS-90 the listener answers `SELECT @@GLOBAL.GTID_MODE` from the storage's replication mode, which decides how PBS resumes from its source, not what the stored events are. A position-mode storage of a GTID source holds GTID_LOG events.
issues.fix: Derive the reported GTID_MODE from the stored stream: ON when the stored binlogs contain GTID_LOG / GTID_TAGGED_LOG events or a non-empty PREVIOUS_GTIDS set, OFF when they hold only ANONYMOUS_GTID events (or add a replication_source.gtid_mode setting).
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::ReplicaOfPositionStorageOfGtidSourceMySQL'` must pass; `ReplicaOfListenerMatchesSourceMySQL` and `ReplicaOfPositionStorageGtidOffMySQL` must keep passing.
issues.impact: Every position-mode Binlog Server of a GTID source (the default from MySQL 9.7) used as a replication source: no MySQL replica with default settings can replicate from it. A clear error, no data loss.

issues.title: Interrupted creation of a non-consecutive binlog leaves an unopenable storage
issues.summary: The startup recovery only recognises the leftover of an interrupted creation of the binlog that follows the last indexed one. In GTID mode the source can start at a later binlog, so a crash or full disk while creating it leaves an object that every later fetch / pull refuses ("not referenced in the binlog index").
issues.description:
Jenkins #29, `DiskFullLeavesStorageConsistentMySQL` (reported as a regression of PBT-038): GTID mode; the storage holds binlog.000001 as the magic only (PBT-020); the source runs FLUSH BINARY LOGS, a rolled back transaction and FLUSH BINARY LOGS, so binlog.000002 has no transaction and binlog.000003 is current; fetch with a file size limit of 0 (full disk) fails while creating binlog.000003 (MySQL's auto-positioning starts at the newest binlog whose PREVIOUS_GTIDS is covered); fetch with space again fails with "storage contains an object that is not referenced in the binlog index". Not yet reproduced in the sandbox.

2026-11-24: the GTID-only path (DiskFullLeavesStorageConsistentMySQL, a non-consecutive binlog after GTID auto-positioning) is closed as obsolete with rewrite mode. The bug itself stays open: the storage recovery still knows only the binlog that follows the last indexed one (CrashWhileCreatingLaterBinlogIsRecovered fails).
issues.root_cause: Verified in `src/binsrv/storage_core.cpp`, `storage_core::collect_interrupted_rotation_objects()`: it checks only `binlog_records_.back().name.next()` (the next sequence number) for a data / metadata object holding no events. `storage_core::open_binlog()` accepts any later name, so an interrupted creation of binlog.000003 after binlog.000001 is not recognised and the general check reports the unindexed object. PBS-59 / PBS-109 (PBT-038 fixed) cover the consecutive case only.
issues.fix: Treat any unindexed binlog object with a sequence number above the last indexed one and no events (data at most the magic, metadata of size 4 or empty) as the leftover of an interrupted creation - or record the name being created (e.g. in metadata.json) before creating its objects.
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::DiskFullLeavesStorageConsistentMySQL'` must pass (also with PBT_REPRODUCE set to the Jenkins #29 seed); `UnindexedObjectsFollowTheRulesMySQL` and `CrashWhileCreatingBinlogIsRecovered` must keep passing (the latter could draw a non-consecutive name).
issues.impact: A full disk, a crash or an S3 error exactly while a GTID-mode fetch / pull creates a binlog whose number skips binlogs without transactions (after FLUSH BINARY LOGS on an idle source, server restarts): collection stops until someone deletes the object by hand.

issues.title: Connection failures are logged without their reason
issues.summary: When fetch or pull cannot connect to the MySQL source, the log says only "unable to establish connection to mysql server", not the reason the client library reports (access denied, connection refused, TLS verification failed). Operators cannot tell a wrong password from a network or certificate problem.
issues.description: D36, `ConnectionFailureIsExplainedInLogMySQL`: fetch with a wrong password, a port nothing listens on, ssl mode verify_ca with another CA, or an account requiring TLS with ssl mode disabled must fail and name the reason in its log. Jenkins #30 (first run): fails; the smallest case is a wrong password - the log has no "Access denied". fetch fails correctly (exit code 1, no crash).
issues.root_cause: Hrvoje's analysis (ticket 47, PBS-121): `collector_context::open_connection_and_switch_to_replication()` catches the connection exception and logs a fixed message without the exception's text (the MySQL client error), then returns false.
issues.fix: Include the exception text (mysql_error / mysql_errno from easymysql) in the logged error, e.g. "unable to establish connection to mysql server: Access denied for user ... (1045)".
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::ConnectionFailureIsExplainedInLogMySQL'` must pass for every failure kind.

issues.title: Normal client disconnects are logged at error level
issues.summary: Every client of the listener that ends its dump normally (mysqlbinlog finishing, a replica reconnecting) produces an error-level line ("system error caught in session ...: End of file"), which buries real errors and trips log-based alerting.
issues.description: D36, `NormalClientDisconnectIsNotAnErrorMySQL`: 1 - 3 dumps from the listener that end normally (a non-blocking dump at its end, a blocking dump the client closes); pull's log must have no error-level line. Jenkins #30 (first run): fails. Earlier listener logs show the lines: "[  error] net : system error caught in session ...: asio.misc:2" (End of file).
issues.root_cause: Hrvoje's analysis (ticket 42, PBS-115): `network_service::session()` catches `boost::system::system_error` and logs every one at error level, including `asio::error::eof` / connection reset when the client closes its connection.
issues.fix: Treat eof / connection_reset / broken_pipe after a completed or idle dump as a normal end of the session (info or debug level); keep error level for other system errors.

issues.title: Running out of file descriptors ends the listener's accept loop for good
issues.summary: Once pull runs out of file descriptors, the replication source stops accepting connections for ever while pull keeps running (so no supervisor restarts it). Idle connections that never log in are enough - no credentials needed.
issues.description: D38, `ListenerRecoversFromDescriptorExhaustionMySQL`: pull's soft RLIMIT_NOFILE is lowered (prlimit) to its open descriptors + 8 - 64; that many + 1 - 64 idle connections are opened to the listener, held 0 - 2 s and closed; the limit is kept or restored. A non-blocking dump must then succeed within 15 s. Jenkins #32 (first run): fails - no dump connects again ("Lost connection"), pull is still running.
issues.root_cause: `network_service::listener()` (src/minimysql/network_service.cpp): `async_accept` errors other than `operation_aborted` / `bad_descriptor` are raised as `boost::system::system_error`; EMFILE ends the loop through `handle_exception("listener")`. Nothing limits the number of sessions, and a session that never logs in holds its socket until read_timeout.
issues.fix: On EMFILE / ENFILE / ENOBUFS / ENOMEM / ECONNABORTED: log, back off briefly (e.g. 100 ms with back-off) and keep accepting. Limit concurrent (not yet authenticated) sessions, possibly per address, with a shorter login timeout. If the accept loop ever ends on an error, end the process so a supervisor restarts it.
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::ListenerRecoversFromDescriptorExhaustionMySQL'` must pass.
issues.impact: Availability: anyone who can reach the listener port can stop replicas and point-in-time recovery from being served until pull is restarted; a legitimate reconnect burst against a low limit does the same. Hrvoje's ticket 55.

issues.title: An encrypted storage started without its encryption section writes new binlogs in plaintext
issues.summary: With the keyring kept (needed to read the existing binlogs) but the storage.encryption section dropped, PBS opens an encrypted storage without complaint and writes every new binlog unencrypted; metadata.json keeps saying "generic" and nothing is logged.
issues.description: D39, `StorageStartedWithoutEncryptionKeepsEncrypting`: 1 - 2 encrypted binlogs (any compatible KEK / data cipher), storage reopened with the keyring but without storage.encryption: it must refuse to start or keep encrypting. Jenkins #32 (first run): fails - the next binlog (binlog.000002) is plaintext. Decision 2026-11-16: switching encryption off silently is a bug (as in Hrvoje's ticket 54); `EncryptionCanBeToggledButNeedsTheKek` became `EncryptionCanBeEnabledButNeedsTheKek` (off -> on only; passes).
issues.root_cause: `storage_core::validate_metadata()` compares the configured encryption format with the one in metadata.json only when both are set; `generate_binlog_encryption_record()` returns nothing without an active KEK.
issues.fix: Treat "format in metadata, none in the configuration" as an error (or keep encrypting with the last KEK and warn). If disabling encryption is supported, require an explicit setting and record in metadata.json from which binlog the storage is unencrypted.
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'storage_property_test::StorageStartedWithoutEncryptionKeepsEncrypting'` must pass.
issues.impact: A configuration-management mistake silently removes encryption at rest for all future binlogs; someone who can edit the configuration but not read the keyring can turn it off. Hrvoje's ticket 54.

issues.title: Encrypted binlog data and metadata are not authenticated
issues.summary: Storage encryption is CTR without a MAC, and the binlog metadata is not authenticated: someone who can write the storage but has no key can change stored events (XOR into the ciphertext) or replace a binlog with plaintext of their choosing, and PBS serves it without an error.
issues.description: D40: `TamperedEncryptedBinlogIsDetected` - 1 - 4 bytes after the magic XORed in the ciphertext file; a restarted storage must not return the changed data without an error. Jenkins #32: fails at once (1 byte XORed with 01 at offset 4 of a 5-byte binlog). `EncryptedBinlogStrippedOfEncryptionIsNotServed` - a binlog after an encrypted one replaced with same-size plaintext and its encryption record removed from <binlog>.json; it must not be served. Jenkins #32: served as plaintext without an error.
issues.root_cause: `encryption_config.cpp` accepts only CTR data ciphers; only the file key envelope has a GCM tag; the binlog metadata records sizes, not a MAC, and is itself unauthenticated. CRC32 footers can be patched to match a change (CRC32 is affine).
issues.fix: Authenticate the data per chunk / checkpoint (HMAC keyed from the file key, recorded in the binlog metadata, or an AEAD mode with per-chunk tags; needs a storage format version) and authenticate the metadata (or record from which binlog the storage is encrypted). Until then document encryption as confidentiality-only.
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'storage_property_test::*Encrypted*'` must pass.
issues.impact: Anyone with write access to the storage (shared file system, misconfigured bucket policy, restored backup) can alter replicated changes without the keyring; replicas and point-in-time recovery apply them. Hrvoje's ticket 53 (PBS-126).

issues.title: The listener sends stored events without verifying their CRC32
issues.summary: An event changed in the storage (one body byte, so its CRC32 no longer matches) is streamed to clients as it is: the sender splits blocks by event size only, although the binlog's FORMAT_DESCRIPTION announces CRC32.
issues.description: D40, `ListenerDoesNotServeCorruptedEventsMySQL`: after fetch, one body byte of a stored event (not the header, footer or a FORMAT_DESCRIPTION) changed in the storage file (plain or encrypted); pull must refuse the storage or a non-blocking dump of that binlog must not receive the event. Jenkins #32 (first run): fails - the corrupted event is sent without an error.
issues.root_cause: `indexed_event_block` indexes events by size only (indexed_event_block.cpp: "TODO: consider performing checksum validation here"); only the FORMAT_DESCRIPTION's checksum is verified.
issues.fix: Verify each event's CRC32 in the sender when the FORMAT_DESCRIPTION announces CRC32 and end the dump with an error. This catches accidental corruption and blind changes, not a deliberately patched footer (see PBT-067).
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::ListenerDoesNotServeCorruptedEventsMySQL'` must pass.
issues.impact: Corrupted data reaches clients; MySQL replicas verify event checksums when they receive them, but point-in-time recovery with mysqlbinlog and other clients may not. Hrvoje's ticket 53, the sender part.

issues.title: A storage does not record its source: a reset or different source is followed silently
issues.summary: The storage metadata records no server_uuid or binlog lineage. After the source resets its binary logs, or fetch is pointed at a different server, fetch resumes at the stored binlog name and offset; when the new binlog reaches that offset it exits 0 and the storage is not a copy of any server.
issues.description:
D41, `SourceChangeIsNotFollowedSilentlyMySQL`: after a fetch, the source resets its binary logs (RESET BINARY LOGS AND GTIDS / RESET MASTER) or fetch is pointed at a different, never-replicated server; 1 - 6 operations and 1 - 30 rows on it; fetch must refuse and leave the storage as it was, or exit 0 with an exact copy of the current source. Jenkins #33 (first run) fails in its first case: position mode, 1 insert fetched (binlog.000001, 450 bytes), RESET BINARY LOGS AND GTIDS, 1 insert - the new binlog.000001 also has 450 bytes, fetch resumes at binlog.000001:450, logs "successfully fetched everything" and exits 0; the stored binlog.000001 still holds the old data (differs from offset 219). With a shorter new binlog the storage is wedged instead (every fetch exits 1, the message only names an offset).

Jenkins #39: also through a failover in position mode (`FailoverPositionModeIsRefusedMySQL`, reported as new): the storage's newest binlog.000002 is stored as the magic only (PBT-020) and the promoted replica, a different server, has a binlog.000002 too - fetch resumes at binlog.000002:4 and exits 0. Second known_bugs row for PBT-069.
issues.root_cause: `storage_metadata` (metadata.json) holds only version, mode and encryption; the collector resumes from the stored binlog name / position (position mode) or the stored GTID set (GTID mode) and never checks the source's server_uuid. In GTID mode a reset source counts GTIDs from 1 again with the same server_uuid, so overlapping GTIDs look already stored.
issues.fix: Record the source's server_uuid (and a lineage marker, e.g. the first binlog's FORMAT_DESCRIPTION timestamp / PREVIOUS_GTIDS) in the storage metadata when the storage is first written; on every connect compare it and refuse a mismatch with a clear message. Detect a restarted binlog sequence (the source's binlog.000001 shorter than or different from the stored one).
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::SourceChangeIsNotFollowedSilentlyMySQL'` must pass.
issues.impact: A routine operation (a GTID reset, a promotion of another server) leaves a silently wrong backup: the operator believes the binlogs are captured while the storage holds another history. Hrvoje's ticket 25.

issues.title: Storage files take their mode from the umask
issues.summary: Binlog data, binlog metadata, binlog.index and metadata.json are created 0666 & ~umask: world-readable under umask 022, world-writable under 000. MySQL creates its binlogs 0640 whatever the umask.
issues.description: D44, `StorageFilesAreNotWorldAccessible`: umask 000 / 002 / 022 / 027, a plain or encrypted storage with 1 - 3 binlogs; no storage object may have a permission for others or group write. Jenkins #36 (first run): fails at umask 000 - binlog.index, metadata.json, binlog.000001 and binlog.000001.json are 0666.
issues.root_cause: The filesystem backend creates binlog data with std::ofstream and the other objects with a write-then-rename helper, never with an explicit mode (filesystem_storage_backend.cpp: "TODO: check permissions here").
issues.fix: Create files with an explicit mode (open(2) with 0640, or std::filesystem::permissions right after creating them); optionally warn when the storage directory is group- or world-writable.
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'storage_property_test::StorageFilesAreNotWorldAccessible'` must pass.
issues.impact: Binlogs hold every change of the source (personal data, sometimes credentials): any local user can read an unencrypted storage, and under a permissive umask rewrite it. Hrvoje's ticket 56.

issues.title: The filesystem storage writes through symlinks planted in the storage directory
issues.summary: Symlinks planted under the names PBS writes next (the next binlog, its .json.tmp, binlog.index.tmp) are followed: PBS overwrites the files they point to.

issues.title: A long SET statement from a logged-in client crashes pull
issues.summary: Every statement goes through std::regex_search with the handshake patterns; libstdc++'s regex executor recurses per character, so a SET statement with a run of 20,000 - 40,000+ spaces, tabs, line feeds or digits overflows the stack and the whole pull process dies (SIGSEGV), collector included.
issues.description: D47, `ListenerSurvivesLongStatementsMySQL`: a client logged in with the listener's account sends SET + a run of 1,000 - 300,000 whitespace characters, or SET @master_heartbeat_period= + digits; pull must keep running and serve a new dump. Jenkins #36 (first run): fails - pull terminated after a 40,029-byte statement (heartbeat period + 40,000 digits).
issues.root_cause: network_service.cpp passes the whole COM_QUERY (up to 16 MiB) to std::regex_search for each pattern of handshake_query_patterns.hpp (\s+, \s*, [0-9]+); no length limit; the listener runs on the process's main io_context.
issues.fix: Refuse statements longer than a few KiB before matching (no handshake statement is longer), or parse the handshake statements by hand.
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::ListenerSurvivesLongStatementsMySQL'` must pass.
issues.impact: One packet from any client with the replication credentials stops the Binlog Server: backup and every replica. Hrvoje's ticket 72 (PBS-140).

issues.title: Rewrite mode trusts the stored GTID set: edited metadata makes fetch skip transactions
issues.summary: The resume set is the newest binlog's previous_gtids + added_gtids from its unauthenticated metadata; GTIDs added there are never requested and fetch exits 0 without ever storing those transactions. Since 4717df9 every GTID storage is in rewrite mode.
issues.description: D48, `EditedStoredGtidsDoNotSkipTransactionsMySQL`: a rewrite-mode storage of 2 - 6 transactions; 1 - 3 future GTIDs added to the newest binlog's added_gtids; the source commits them (+ 0 - 2). Jenkins #36 (first run): fails - fetch exits 0 and transaction :3 is never stored.
issues.root_cause: The collector asks for everything not in the stored set (storage_core / collector_context) and in rewrite mode stamps its own positions, so the position check that catches this without rewrite always holds; nothing compares an arriving GTID with the stored events.
issues.fix: Check each arriving GTID against the stored set (refuse one already stored or out of order within its UUID) and derive / verify the resume set from the stored events, not from metadata alone.
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::EditedStoredGtidsDoNotSkipTransactionsMySQL'` must pass.
issues.impact: Anyone who can write the storage, without a key, can make the backup drop chosen future transactions while every run reports success. Hrvoje's ticket 81 (PBS-147).

issues.title: A KEK id is not bound to its key bytes
issues.summary: A keyring whose record for the active KEK id holds other bytes is accepted, and with a CTR / CBC / ECB KEK new file keys are wrapped with them: new data can be read only with the replaced bytes, and every run reports success.
issues.description: D49, `ReplacedKekBytesAreRefused`: an encrypted storage with 1 - 2 binlogs; the keyring's bytes for the active KEK id replaced (same id and cipher); the next binlog written must be refused or readable with the original keyring. Jenkins #36 (first run): fails - binlog.000003 is written without an error and cannot be read with the original keyring.
issues.root_cause: storage_core checks only that the KEK id exists; no key check value is stored, and only a GCM KEK authenticates the wrapped file key.
issues.fix: Store a key check value per KEK id (e.g. an HMAC of a fixed label under the KEK) in metadata.json and each encryption record, verify it when the keyring is loaded and before any append; wrap file keys with an authenticated mode whatever the KEK's cipher.
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'storage_property_test::ReplacedKekBytesAreRefused'` must pass.

issues.title: rewrite.file_size is not honoured across fetch runs or reconnects
issues.summary: After a (re)connect, rewrite mode appends the first transaction to the current binlog whatever its size; the size is checked only at the next transaction boundary of the same session. A fetch run (cron) or a pull reconnect that gets one transaction never rotates, so the binlog grows without bound.
issues.description: Found in Jenkins #39 by `InterruptedPurgeIsRecoveredMySQL`, which needs two stored binlogs: GTID mode (always rewrite mode since 4717df9), file_size 4K, then 20 fetch runs of one 5000-byte row each - still a single binlog of about 100 KB. D50 `RewriteFileSizeIsHonouredAcrossFetchesMySQL` (file_size 1K / 4K, 2 - 8 fetch runs of 1 - 2 transactions): no transaction but a binlog's first may start at or beyond file_size. Not in Hrvoje's list. Jenkins #40: D50 confirms it in its first run (file_size 1K, a transaction starting at rw.000001:1040).
issues.root_cause: `collector_context::process_event_in_rewrite_mode()`: for the first event after a reconnect (`context.is_fresh()`) on a non-empty storage it reopens `storage_->get_current_binlog_name()`; the rotation condition `is_at_transaction_boundary() && get_current_position() >= file_size` is evaluated only for later events of the session.
issues.fix: On the first event after a reconnect, rotate when the current binlog has already reached file_size (emit the ROTATE / FORMAT_DESCRIPTION / PREVIOUS_GTIDS of the next binlog), as at a transaction boundary.
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::RewriteFileSizeIsHonouredAcrossFetchesMySQL'` must pass.
issues.impact: Binlog files grow without bound for fetch run from cron with a low transaction rate (or a pull that reconnects often): purge_binlogs cannot free space below one huge binlog, and replicas / point-in-time recovery read much larger files than configured.

issues.title: Removing the encryption record from the last binlog makes PBS append plaintext
issues.summary: The encryption record of a binlog lives in its unauthenticated metadata. With it removed from the newest binlog's .json, a writer that resumes that binlog appends plaintext to an encrypted storage, and saves the metadata again without a record.
issues.description: D51, `StrippedEncryptionRecordDoesNotTurnOffEncryption`: an encrypted storage (storage.encryption still configured) with 1 - 2 binlogs; the newest binlog's encryption record removed; the writer resumes it (open_binlog of the same name) and appends 8 - 32 bytes - must be refused or not stored in plaintext. Jenkins #42 (first run): fails - with the record removed from binlog.000001.json, 8 appended bytes are stored in plaintext. The read side is PBT-067 (EncryptedBinlogStrippedOfEncryptionIsNotServed).
issues.root_cause: `storage_core::validate_binlog_encryption_record()` checks a record only when it is present, also when storage.encryption is configured and metadata.json says generic; `write_data_to_stream()` writes plaintext when the loaded record is missing.
issues.fix: Refuse a binlog without an encryption record in a storage that records an encryption format (or start a new, encrypted binlog instead of appending); authenticate the metadata (PBT-067).
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'storage_property_test::StrippedEncryptionRecordDoesNotTurnOffEncryption'` must pass.
issues.impact: Someone who can only write the storage turns off encryption at rest for every byte PBS receives afterwards in that binlog, without any key and without any sign. Hrvoje's ticket 62 (PBS-136).

issues.description: D52, `ListenerLogIsNotForgeableMySQL`: a client logged in with the replication account sends a statement or a dump of a binlog name carrying LF / CR LF / lone CR + a forged log line, an ANSI escape, a NUL or 1 MiB of text. issues.title: Gapped GTIDs make a rewrite-mode storage grow quadratically
issues.summary: Every binlog rewrite mode starts begins with a PREVIOUS_GTIDS_LOG event of the storage's whole GTID set; each gap in the GTIDs adds an interval, and once the event alone exceeds file_size every transaction starts a new binlog carrying the whole set again.
issues.description: D53, `GappedGtidsDoNotGrowStorageQuadraticallyMySQL`: 300 - 600 one-row transactions with GTIDs 1, 3, 5, ... (SET gtid_next) on one source binlog; a rewrite-mode storage with file_size 4K may hold at most 4 x the source's bytes + 64 KiB. Jenkins #42 (first run): fails at the smallest size - 300 gapped transactions, 85,058 source bytes, stored as 507,030 bytes in 111 binlogs.
issues.root_cause: `collector_context` generates the PREVIOUS_GTIDS_LOG of each new rewrite-mode binlog from the whole stored set and rotates by file_size including that preamble; every binlog's metadata holds a full previous_gtids, all loaded at start.
issues.fix: Rotate only when a binlog holds more than its preamble; bound the per-binlog GTID data (e.g. store the set once / merge intervals); consider refusing or warning on extreme interval counts.
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::GappedGtidsDoNotGrowStorageQuadraticallyMySQL'` must pass.
issues.impact: A source (or a man in the middle) with gapped GTIDs makes the storage, memory and start-up time grow quadratically until list / fetch fail with bad_alloc. Hrvoje's ticket 88 (PBS-164): 6,000 transactions -> 362 MiB.

issues.title: A lowered transaction_length makes PBS store part of a transaction as all of it
issues.summary: PBS takes the end of a transaction only from the transaction_length of its GTID event. A man in the middle between PBS and its source who lowers that number (and fixes the CRC32) makes PBS store the first events of a transaction - down to the GTID event alone - as a complete transaction.
issues.description: D55, `LoweredTransactionLengthIsNotStoredMySQL`: a proxy between PBS and the source lowers the transaction_length of one transaction to end after GTID, BEGIN, TABLE_MAP or the first ROWS event (or 1 byte before its true end), fixes the CRC32, and sends the rest, ends the dump, closes the connection or leaves the rest out; the attacked run is fetch or pull (checkpoint_size 1). The storage may hold only complete transactions of the source, and an honest fetch afterwards must complete it. Jenkins #43 (first run): fails in its first case - position mode, pull: transaction_length 923 lowered to 79, all 5 events sent; the storage keeps the GTID event alone (with the lowered length) as the transaction, and pull exits 1. D54 (the same cuts without a lie: EOF packet, closed connection, half an event) passes.
issues.root_cause: `reader_context` (start / update / finish_transaction) treats the declared transaction_length as the transaction's end; what lies before such a boundary is written by checkpoints, the end of a run and the error paths, and in GTID mode recorded as a stored GTID. Nothing checks that the event at the declared end actually ends a transaction (XID / COMMIT / DDL) or that the next event starts one.
issues.fix: Before storing a transaction, check that it ends where it says: the last event is XID, a COMMIT query, or a DDL / non-transactional statement, and the next event starts a transaction; refuse the dump otherwise. Use TLS with verification to the source (Hrvoje's ticket 60).
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::LoweredTransactionLengthIsNotStoredMySQL'` must pass.
issues.impact: A man in the middle (or a buggy source) makes PBS store a stub transaction: Hrvoje's ticket 82 - in position and GTID mode every later run then exits 1, rewrite mode goes on without the rows, and MySQL 8.4 replicas reading the stub abort.

issues.title: The collector's memory grows with what it collects
issues.summary: storage::write_event() keeps every event since the last checkpoint in memory (event_buffer_), and an unfinished transaction always: without checkpoint settings a whole binlog (up to max_binlog_size, 1 GiB) is held in memory, and a large transaction - or one that never ends - grows it without limit.
issues.description: D56, `CollectorMemoryDoesNotGrowWithDataMySQL`: the source writes 256 or 384 MiB into one binlog (1 MiB transactions or one transaction of 1 MiB rows); a fetch of it (no checkpoint settings, checkpoint_size 1M or checkpoint_interval 1s; rewrite file_size 1G) may use at most 96 MiB more peak RSS (VmHWM) than a fetch of one 1 MiB transaction (ASan quarantine 1 MiB). Jenkins #44 (first run): fails in its first case - position mode, no checkpoint settings, 256 transactions of 1 MiB: peak RSS 125 MiB fetching 1 MiB, 641 MiB fetching the 256 MiB (+516 MiB, about twice the data).
issues.root_cause: `storage::write_event()` appends every event to `event_buffer_` and writes it to the backend only at a checkpoint (checkpoint_size / checkpoint_interval) or when the binlog is closed; the part after the last transaction boundary always stays buffered.
issues.fix: Write complete transactions to the backend (or an unpublished part of the object) as they arrive and keep only the checkpoint bookkeeping in memory; spill an unfinished transaction to a temporary file; refuse a transaction beyond a configured limit.
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::CollectorMemoryDoesNotGrowWithDataMySQL'` must pass.
issues.impact: Hrvoje's ticket 87 (PBS-163): a large binlog from an honest source without checkpoint settings, a large transaction, or a source / man in the middle that never ends a transaction makes fetch / pull die with std::bad_alloc (or the host run out of memory).

issues.title: By default the connection to the source is not verified
issues.summary: Without an `ssl` section PBS connects like --ssl-mode=PREFERRED: any certificate is accepted, and it falls back to plaintext when the server (or a man in the middle that clears CLIENT_SSL) offers no TLS. A man in the middle captures the replication password and can rewrite the binlog stream (PBT-079, PBT-080).
issues.description: D57, `UnverifiedSourceIsRefusedByDefaultMySQL`: without an `ssl` section, fetch must refuse a source whose identity it has not verified - a certificate of the test CA (not configured as trusted) for 127.0.0.1 or for another name, or no TLS at all. Jenkins #44 (first run): fails in its first case - the certificate for 127.0.0.1 is accepted and fetch exits 0.
issues.root_cause: `connection::process_ssl_config()` is called only when an `ssl` section exists; otherwise libmysqlclient's default (SSL_MODE_PREFERRED, no verification) applies.
issues.fix: Default to verify_identity (system or configured CA), or refuse to start without an explicit `ssl` section; document that preferred / required do not authenticate the source.
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::UnverifiedSourceIsRefusedByDefaultMySQL'` must pass (and D22's model of the default changes with the fix).
issues.impact: Hrvoje's ticket 60 (PBS-134): with the default configuration a man in the middle captures the replication password (caching_sha2_password full authentication over its own TLS) and controls what is stored and served.

issues.title: A binlog name chosen by the source overwrites stored files
issues.summary: composite_binlog_name::parse() rejects a '/' but keeps any other byte, and the filesystem backend hands the name to the C file API, which stops at a NUL byte: a source (or a man in the middle on an unverified connection) that names its next binlog 'binlog.000001\0.N' makes PBS reopen and truncate binlog.000001; 'metadata.json\0.N', 'binlog.index\0.N' and a line feed in the name damage the storage metadata.
issues.description: D58, `SourceBinlogNamesDoNotTouchOtherFilesMySQL`: names with a NUL byte, a line feed, a base name '..' or of 3000 bytes. A proxy between PBS and the source (TLS off, PBT-082) renames the source's next binlog in its ROTATE events (size, log_pos, CRC32 fixed) during a position-mode fetch; afterwards every binlog stored before must keep its data, metadata.json stay unchanged, binlog.index only grow, no binlog hold two FORMAT_DESCRIPTION events, the storage open and list no name with a control character, and a direct fetch not refuse the storage. Jenkins #46 (first run): fails in its first case - 'binlog.000001\0.000002' truncates binlog.000001 from 452 to 125 bytes, and fetch exits 0.
issues.root_cause: The binlog name from a ROTATE event is used as an object name without validation beyond '/'; std::ofstream / open() see the name up to its first NUL byte, and binlog.index is a line-based file.
issues.fix: Accept only names <base>.<digits> whose base is printable, without '/', NUL or line breaks and not '.' / '..'; refuse a name that is not the stored binlog's successor (position mode).
issues.verification: `run_property_tests.py --filter 'mysql_property_test::SourceBinlogNamesDoNotTouchOtherFilesMySQL'` must pass.
issues.impact: Hrvoje's ticket 59 (PBS-131): a compromised source or a man in the middle destroys stored binlogs or makes the storage unopenable, while fetch reports success.

issues.title: A re-announced binlog gets a second preamble appended
issues.summary: A source that announces the binlog being written again (its own name after its closing ROTATE, at position 4) makes PBS append a second FORMAT_DESCRIPTION / PREVIOUS_GTIDS preamble and the following events to the stored binlog, whose log_pos values then no longer match its offsets.
issues.description: D59, `ReannouncedBinlogGetsNoSecondPreambleMySQL`: the source's next binlog renamed to the current one. A proxy between PBS and the source (TLS off, PBT-082) renames the source's next binlog in its ROTATE events (size, log_pos, CRC32 fixed) during a position-mode fetch; afterwards every binlog stored before must keep its data, metadata.json stay unchanged, binlog.index only grow, no binlog hold two FORMAT_DESCRIPTION events, the storage open and list no name with a control character, and a direct fetch not refuse the storage. Jenkins #46 (first run): fails in its first case - binlog.000002 announced as 'binlog.000001': fetch exits 0 and binlog.000001 holds two FORMAT_DESCRIPTION events.
issues.root_cause: The collector opens the named binlog for appending whatever its name, also when it is the binlog just closed.
issues.fix: Refuse a ROTATE to the binlog being written (or to any name that is not its successor) unless it continues at the stored position.

issues.title: A lower binlog sequence number makes the storage unopenable
issues.summary: A binlog name with a lower sequence number than the stored ones is stored; the next start takes it for the leftover of an interrupted purge and refuses the storage.
issues.description: D60, `LowerBinlogSequenceKeepsStorageOpenMySQL`: the source purged its first binlogs before the first fetch, then its next binlog is announced as 'binlog.000002'. A proxy between PBS and the source (TLS off, PBT-082) renames the source's next binlog in its ROTATE events (size, log_pos, CRC32 fixed) during a position-mode fetch; afterwards every binlog stored before must keep its data, metadata.json stay unchanged, binlog.index only grow, no binlog hold two FORMAT_DESCRIPTION events, the storage open and list no name with a control character, and a direct fetch not refuse the storage. Jenkins #46 (first run): fails in its first case - storage starting at binlog.000005, binlog.000006 announced as binlog.000002: fetch exits 0, and the next fetch refuses the storage (binlog index contains a reference to a non-existing object).
issues.root_cause: The collector accepts any sequence number; storage_core::collect_interrupted_purge_objects() treats binlogs numbered below the first indexed one as purge leftovers.
issues.fix: Refuse a name whose sequence number does not follow the stored last one.

only_manish.summary: encode_to() never checks the destination size. Debug builds abort on an assert; Release builds write past the end of the span. uuid::encode_to and tag::encode_to throw instead. No current caller passes a short buffer.

only_manish.title: GTID_LOG body drops fields without immediate_server_version
only_manish.summary: The gtid_log_body constructor accepts original_server_version or commit_group_ticket without an immediate_server_version, but encode_to() silently drops them, so the parsed event differs from the created one.

only_manish.title: Removing an FDE checksum produces an unreadable event
only_manish.summary: materialize(..., force_remove_checksum) strips the footer from a FORMAT_DESCRIPTION event too, while event_view always expects an FDE footer, so the result cannot be parsed. No current caller uses this mode on FDEs.

only_manish.title: Server versions with components of 100+ encode wrongly
only_manish.summary: semantic_version accepts components up to 255, but get_encoded() uses major*10000 + minor*100 + patch, so "8.2.100" encodes as 80300 (8.3.0) and can cross a protocol threshold.

only_manish.title: Metadata with an empty hex value cannot be read back
only_manish.summary: binlog_file_metadata::str() writes an empty hex_value as "", but loading fails with "unable to extract ...data_hex", because hex_value operator>> cannot read an empty word.

only_manish.title: Failed hex_value assignment corrupts the value
only_manish.summary: Assigning a malformed even-length hex string throws, but the object was already resized and partly overwritten. No strong exception guarantee.

only_manish.title: flag_set default constructor leaves bits uninitialized
only_manish.summary: The bits_ member has no initializer, so a default-initialized flag_set holds garbage. Every current use is value-initialized, so the bug is latent.

only_manish.title: reader_context grammar comment says PREVIOUS_GTIDS is optional
only_manish.summary: The state-machine comment marks PREVIOUS_GTIDS_LOG as optional, but the code requires it after a non-info-only FDE. Only the comment is wrong.

only_manish.title: Readable CRC prints as 000x1234
only_manish.summary: get_readable_crc_from_raw() combines showbase with setfill and setw, so the zero padding goes before the 0x prefix. Affects debug logs only.

only_manish.title: Printing a binlog name leaves the stream fill changed
only_manish.summary: operator<< for composite_binlog_name sets setfill('0') and never restores it, so later padded output on the same stream is zero-filled.
